overview.text:
Uttarakhand is a Himalayan state of 53,483 sq km between Himachal Pradesh, Tibet, Nepal and Uttar Pradesh — about 86% of it mountains, rising to high peaks and glaciers in the north. It is called Devbhoomi, the land of the gods: the Ganga and the Yamuna both rise here, at Gangotri and Yamunotri, and with Kedarnath and Badrinath these make up the Char Dham pilgrimage. It became India's 27th state in November 2000.

The state has two halves. Garhwal, in the west, runs from Dehradun and the Ganga towns of Haridwar and Rishikesh up to the Char Dham, Auli and the Valley of Flowers. Kumaon, in the east, is the land of lakes and ridges — Nainital, Bhimtal, Almora, Ranikhet and Kausani — with Jim Corbett, India's oldest national park, in the foothills and Munsiyari under the high peaks.

Trips mix pilgrimage, hill stations, wildlife and adventure: rafting at Rishikesh, skiing at Auli, kayaking on the lake behind the Tehri Dam — India's tallest — and treks to Tungnath, Kuari Pass and Hemkund Sahib. Twelve national parks and wildlife sanctuaries cover 13.8% of the state.

items.body: Dehradun, the capital, with Mussoorie above it; Haridwar, where the Ganga reaches the plains, and Rishikesh, the yoga and rafting town and starting point for the Char Dham.

items.title: Garhwal: the Char Dham
items.body: Yamunotri and Gangotri in Uttarkashi, Kedarnath above Gaurikund in Rudraprayag, Badrinath in Chamoli — open from late April or May to just after Diwali.

items.title: Chamoli high country
items.body: Auli's ski slopes above Joshimath, the Valley of Flowers and Nanda Devi World Heritage parks, Hemkund Sahib, and Chopta below Tungnath.

items.title: Kumaon lakes
items.body: Nainital and its lake, Bhimtal, Naukuchiatal and Sattal, with Mukteshwar's ridge and Kaichi Dham nearby — reached from Kathgodam.

items.title: Kumaon hills
items.body: Almora, the old Chand capital, Ranikhet's cantonment, Kausani's Himalayan view, Binsar and Jageshwar.

items.title: Corbett and the foothills
items.body: Jim Corbett National Park near Ramnagar, Rajaji near Haridwar, and Lansdowne's Garhwal Rifles cantonment.

items.title: The far east
items.body: Munsiyari under the Panchachuli peaks, in Pithoragarh district — a long drive from Tanakpur or Kathgodam.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Jolly Grant airport serves Dehradun — about 20 km from the city, 35 km from Rishikesh and 37 km from Haridwar — and is the gateway for Garhwal and the Char Dham. Pantnagar is the nearest airport for Kumaon, about 65 km from Nainital, but has few flights. Delhi's international airport is the main gateway from abroad.

By rail: trains barely enter the hills. Dehradun, Haridwar and Rishikesh are the railheads for Garhwal, Kathgodam for Nainital, Ranikhet and Almora, and Tanakpur for Pithoragarh. Haridwar has direct trains to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai.

By road: Dehradun is about 240 km from Delhi, and the drive to Rishikesh takes about 6–7 hours. Uttarakhand Transport Corporation buses are the cheapest way around; Dehradun's ISBT is near Clement Town. For the Char Dham, registration is compulsory for pilgrims and their vehicles.

best_time.text:
March–June: the main hill-station season — Nainital runs around 10–25°C — and the Char Dham opens on Akshaya Tritiya in April or May. May and June are the busiest months on the yatra.

July–August: the monsoon. Heavy rain brings landslides and road blocks in the high valleys, so avoid the Char Dham then. It is, however, when the Valley of Flowers is in bloom (the park opens June to October).

September–November: clear, settled weather after the rains — the best time for views and treks, and the second Char Dham season. The shrines close two days after Diwali.

December–February: winter. Auli's ski slopes are under snow from late November or January to March, Chopta and Tungnath are snowbound, and Mussoorie shows its 'winterline' sunsets. The high shrines are closed from November to April.

overview.text:
Rishikesh lies on the right bank of the Ganga where it leaves the hills, its banks lined with temples and ashrams. It calls itself the yoga capital of the world and hosts the International Yoga Festival each March; the Beatles came to Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram in 1968, and the Beatles Ashram is now a sight in itself.

Every evening the Ganga aarti is performed at Triveni Ghat. Ram Jhula crosses the river at Sivananda Nagar; the old Lakshman Jhula failed in 2020 and a glass bridge is being built. For adventure, rafting runs Grade I to IV, and Rishikesh has India's highest bungee jump. It is also the starting point for the Char Dham. The town is vegetarian-only and alcohol-free.

overview.text:
Haridwar, Uttarakhand's second-largest city, sits on the right bank of the Ganga at the foot of the Shivaliks. Legend says drops of amrita fell at Brahma Kund on Har ki Pauri, the most sacred ghat, where the evening aarti with huge flaming lamps draws crowds every night.

Mansa Devi on Bilwa Parvat, Chandi Devi on Neel Parvat and Maya Devi form the city's trio of Siddhpeeth temples. Haridwar hosts the Kumbh Mela every 12 years and the Ardh Kumbh every six, and it is the centre of the Kanwar pilgrimage in Shravan. Rajaji National Park's Shivalik forests are close by.

overview.text:
Dehradun, the state's winter capital, spreads across the Doon Valley below Mussoorie. It is a city of institutions — the Forest Research Institute, the Survey of India and the Indian Military Academy — and the FRI's grand Greco-Roman building, with six forest museums, is its best-known sight.

Just outside the city are Robber's Cave, where a stream vanishes underground, the sulphur springs of Sahastradhara and the Tapkeshwar cave temple. Mindrolling Monastery is one of India's major Buddhist centres. Shop at Paltan Bazaar by the Clock Tower; Rajpur Road has the bars.

overview.text:
Mussoorie, the 'Queen of the Hills', sits at about 2,000 m on a ridge with the Doon Valley below and the snow ranges to the north-east; Landour and its cantonment adjoin it. Mall Road is the heart of town.

A ropeway climbs to Gun Hill (2,122 m), and Lal Tibba in Landour is the highest point, with views of the Badrinath, Kedarnath, Bandarpunch and Nanda Devi peaks. Kempty Falls is on the Yamunotri road, and Sir George Everest's House (Park Estate) dates from 1832. From October to February, sunsets can show the 'winterline'. Mussoorie is also a gateway to Gangotri and Yamunotri, and Dhanaulti is 24 km away.

overview.text:
Nainital, at 1,938 m, wraps round an eye-shaped lake in the Kumaon foothills. It is the headquarters of Kumaon division and the seat of the state High Court, and gives its name to India's 'Lake District'.

Row across Naini Lake with a local oarsman; the Naina Devi temple stands at its northern end. Naina Peak (2,611 m), 6 km away, is the highest point — ponies go up from Snow View or Barapathar — and Tiffin Top (Dorothy's Seat) is 4 km from town. Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal are short drives away, and Kaichi Dham is on the Almora road.

Mukteshwar is a village on a high Kumaon ridge, 51 km from Nainital, ringed by fruit orchards and conifer forest. An old Shiva temple stands on a rock at the top, and the long view takes in the Himalayan ranges.

The British set up a research laboratory here in 1893; it is now the hill campus of the Indian Veterinary Research Institute, whose museum keeps Robert Koch's microscope. Next to the temple, the cliffs of Chauli ki Jali are used for rock climbing and rappelling. Jim Corbett knew the place as Muktesar.

overview.text:
Almora sits on a ridge at the southern edge of the Kumaon hills. Founded in 1568, it was the seat of the Chand kings and is still called the cultural heart of Kumaon; every September the five-day Nanda Devi Mela fills the town.

Around it are some of Uttarakhand's oldest shrines: Kasar Devi (2nd century CE), where Vivekananda came and the 1960s hippie trail followed; the 124 temples of Jageshwar; and Katarmal, Kumaon's only sun temple. Binsar's oak forest, with over 200 bird species, is on a ridge to the north. In town, Lala Bazaar is the old market.

Kausani stands at 1,890 m on a pine ridge facing a 300-km line of snow peaks — Trishul, Nanda Devi and Panchachuli among them. Gandhi, who stayed 12 days in 1929, called it the 'Switzerland of India'; the guest house where he wrote is now the Anasakti Ashram. The Hindi poet Sumitranandan Pant was born here.

Come for the sunrise on the peaks, then visit the tea estate on the Bageshwar road and the shawl weavers, or walk 5 km to Pinnath. Baijnath's temple group on the Gomti is 19 km away. Summers are mild (10–26°C) and winters cold (2–15°C).

overview.text:
Corbett was set up in 1936 as India's first national park and was the first under Project Tiger. Its 520.8 sq km of hills, river belts, grassland and sal forest hold 50 mammal, 580 bird and 25 reptile species; Ramnagar is the nearest town.

Dhikala, on the edge of the Patli Dun valley, has an old forest rest house. The main season has long run from 15 November to 15 June, and the late dry season — April to mid-June — gives the best chance of a tiger. Book safaris and forest stays only on the official corbettgov.org site, with the same ID you will show at the gate.

items.body: Take a jeep safari into the tiger reserve.
Stay overnight at Dhikala forest rest house (book early).
Go birding — 580 species are recorded.
Visit in April–June for the best tiger chances.

how_to_reach.text: Pantnagar airport is about 120 km away. The overnight Ranikhet Express from Delhi carries through coaches to Ramnagar. Same-day online safari booking closes at 6:30 am for mornings and 4 pm for afternoons. Human–animal conflict helpline: 1800 890 1975.

overview.text:
Lansdowne, at about 1,700 m in Pauri Garhwal, was founded as a cantonment in 1887 and is still the regimental centre of the Garhwal Rifles, which keeps it small and tidy. The regimental museum tells the Rifles' story; to visit the War Memorial you need prior military permission.

Walk to Tip-in-Top beside St Mary's Church (built in 1895, now a museum), trek 2 km to the balanced rocks of Bhim Pakora, or row on Bhulla Tal. October brings the Sharadotsav festival, and winter can bring snow.

Walk to Tip-in-Top by St Mary's Church.

overview.text:
Auli is a high meadow from 2,500 to 3,050 m above Joshimath, run as a ski resort by GMVN, the state tourism corporation. Its 3-km run with a 500-m drop is India's best-known ski slope; snow usually lies deep from January to March, and the slopes are busy from late November. Auli hosted the first South Asian Winter Games in 2011.

The views take in Nanda Devi, Kamet and Dunagiri, and in summer Auli is the start of the Kuari Pass trek and walks to Gorson Bugyal. Joshimath, the base town below, is sinking along its ridge — check local advisories before you go.

items.body: Ski or learn to ski, January–March.
Walk up to Gorson Bugyal.
Trek to Kuari Pass.
Watch the light on Nanda Devi at sunrise.

how_to_reach.text: Auli is 16 km above Joshimath by road; the district also lists a ropeway from Joshimath, so check whether it is running. Joshimath is 253 km from Rishikesh by state bus, and Jolly Grant airport is about 279 km away.

overview.text:
Chopta is a meadow-and-forest halt on the Gopeshwar–Ukhimath road inside the Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary, with views of Trishul, Nanda Devi and Chaukhamba. It is the base for Tungnath (3,680 m), the highest of the Panch Kedar temples and the world's highest Shiva temple, and for the Chandrashila summit just above it — a 4–5 hour round trip.

Birdwatchers come for the forest, and the Deoria Tal lake walk starts from Kund. From December to March, Tungnath and Chandrashila are under snow.

items.body: Trek to Tungnath and on to Chandrashila — start early before cloud builds.
Walk to Deoria Tal from Kund.
Go birdwatching in the forest.

overview.text:
Kedarnath stands at 3,586 m near the head of the Mandakini, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas — the highest of them — and one of the Char Dham. The road ends at Gaurikund, and from there it is a 17-km trek to the temple.

The pilgrimage runs from May to October; in winter the deities are carried down to Ukhimath for six months. The temple came through the 2013 floods when a great boulder shielded it. Avoid July and August, when rain brings landslides. Registration is compulsory, pilgrims are checked at Sonprayag, and helicopter seats are sold only through IRCTC.

items.body: Walk the 17-km trail from Gaurikund.
Join the temple darshan with a slot token.
Visit Ukhimath, where Kedarnath is worshipped in winter.
Carry warm clothes and medicines — the altitude bites.

how_to_reach.text: Rishikesh station is about 210 km from Gaurikund and Jolly Grant airport about 250 km from Kedarnath; buses and taxis run to Gaurikund on NH 107. Yatra control room: 01364-297878 / 297879.

overview.text:
Badrinath stands at 3,133 m beside the Alaknanda in Chamoli district — the Vishnu shrine of the Char Dham, established as a pilgrimage site by Adi Shankara in the ninth century. Pilgrims bathe in the Tapt Kund hot spring before darshan.

The temple is open for about six months, from late April to early November; May–June and September–October are the best months. Mana, 3 km on, is the last village before the border, with Vyas Gufa, and Vasudhara Falls is about 9 km from the temple. Food here is vegetarian, and shops sell rudraksha beads and warm clothes.

items.body: Bathe in Tapt Kund and join darshan.

how_to_reach.text: Fly to Jolly Grant or take the train to Rishikesh or Haridwar, then drive up the Alaknanda valley via Joshimath. Badrinath yatra control room: 01372-251437, toll-free 1077.

overview.text:
Gangotri, at about 3,200 m on the Bhagirathi, is the Char Dham seat of the goddess Ganga; the river takes the name Ganga only at Devprayag, where it meets the Alaknanda. The first temple was built by the Gorkha general Amar Singh Thapa.

The temple closes on Diwali and reopens on Akshaya Tritiya; in winter the goddess is kept at Mukhba village near Harsil. Pilgrims and trekkers continue 19 km to Gomukh, the river's source in the Gangotri Glacier. Harsil, a quiet valley at 2,660 m, is on the way up.

items.body: Attend the evening aarti at the Gangotri temple.
Trek 19 km to Gomukh, the Ganga's glacier source.
Stop in the Harsil valley on the drive up.

how_to_reach.text: Gangotri is 100 km from Uttarkashi on NH 108; Uttarkashi is about 200 km from Dehradun and 250 km from Haridwar, with state buses from Rishikesh and Dehradun. Registration is compulsory.

overview.text:
Yamunotri, at 3,293 m on a flank of Bandarpunch, is the westernmost Char Dham shrine and the seat of the goddess Yamuna, whose source lies in the glaciers above. The district names the temple and the hot springs at Janki Chatti, 7 km away, as its chief draws.

Beside the temple, Surya Kund is the most important hot spring; pilgrims first worship the Divya Shila rock next to it. Yatris are checked at Barkot and Janki Chatti.

items.body: Walk up from Janki Chatti to the temple.
See Surya Kund and the Divya Shila.
Bathe in the hot springs.

how_to_reach.text: Yamunotri is 130 km from Uttarkashi. State buses run between Barkot/Uttarkashi and Rishikesh/Dehradun; Dehradun, about 200 km away, is the nearest railhead.

overview.text:
Munsiyari sits at about 2,200 m at the foot of the high Himalaya in Pithoragarh district, facing the Panchachuli peaks, and is the starting point for treks into the range. It was a depot on the Tibet trade route and the winter home of the Bhotia traders of Johar, who came down from Milam and Laspa when snow closed the high villages.

Around town are Birthi Falls on the Thal road, the Gori river in Johar Valley, a Nanda Devi temple and the Tribal Heritage Museum. Munsiyari is one of the state's ski spots and home to the Pandit Nain Singh Surveyor mountaineering institute.

Ski in winter.

how_to_reach.text: Munsiyari is a long drive into Pithoragarh district. Pithoragarh town is about 138 km from the Tanakpur railhead and 241 km from Pantnagar airport; allow a full day for the mountain roads beyond.
